issue.title: Reduce overhead of parquet metric creation
issue.body:
I wonder if we should apply the same pattern to the other metrics (lazily initialize them) -- if you can get a few percent in this query maybe it would get us a few in the others

_Originally posted by @alamb in https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/21637#discussion_r3243789052_
issue.display_title: Reduce overhead of parquet metric creation

comments.body: I think this will especially help the shorter clickbench queries where the overhead of opening the parquet files is substantial

comments.body:
Update here
* @xudong963 tried this in https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/22353 🏆 

However, upon review I think it turns out we can't use lazy registration as that would change the semantics
- https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/22353#pullrequestreview-4330375309

However, I do think we could reduce the overhead of creating metrics in general by avoiding the string allocations. I am copying my comments from https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/22353#discussion_r3275629426 here as I think they are relevant:

> One challenge is that there are many many new strings with the file name. Maybe it is worth looking into if we could replace the owned string in Label with a Arc<str> (as another PR)
> 
> https://github.com/apache/datafusion/blob/3aefba75be1ec571849136de5f2d575e6c505b7b/datafusion/physical-expr-common/src/metrics/mod.rs#L526-L527
> 
> It might be tricky however, as we would have to retain the special case for `&'static str` 🤔 
> 
> Maybe we could make a new thing instead of Cow like 

```rust
enum ArcCow {
  /// Static string
  Static(&'static str),
  /// Shared arc
  Shared(Arc<str>),
   /// Owned allocation
   Owned(String)
}
```

> With some finagling (like `impl Into<ArcCow>` I suspect we could make it mostly backwards compatible with the existing APIs / callsites 🤔

name: Cow<'static, str>,
value: Cow<'static, str>,

It might be tricky however, as we would have to retain the special case for &'static str 🤔

Maybe we could make a new thing instead of Cow like

enum ArcCow {
  /// Static string
  Static(&'static str),
  /// Shared arc
  Shared(Arc<str>),
   /// Owned allocation
   Owned(String)
}

With some finagling (like impl Into<ArcCow> I suspect we could make it mostly backwards compatible with the existing APIs / callsites 🤔

Maybe

enum SharedStr {
  /// Static string
  Static(&'static str),
  /// Shared arc
  Shared(Arc<str>),
   /// Owned allocation
   Owned(String)
}

And instead of

        let row_groups_pruned_bloom_filter = MetricBuilder::new(metrics)
            .with_new_label("filename", filename.to_string())
            .with_type(MetricType::Summary)
            .pruning_metrics("row_groups_pruned_bloom_filter", partition);

        let limit_pruned_row_groups = MetricBuilder::new(metrics)
            .with_new_label("filename", filename.to_string())
            .with_type(MetricType::Summary)
            .pruning_metrics("limit_pruned_row_groups", partition);

It could look something like

        // Allocate a single copy of the filename
        let shared_filename = Arc::from(filename.as_str());

        let row_groups_pruned_bloom_filter = MetricBuilder::new(metrics)
            .with_new_label("filename", Arc::clone(&shared_filename))     // <---- Only copy Arc here, not new string
            .with_type(MetricType::Summary)
            .pruning_metrics("row_groups_pruned_bloom_filter", partition);  

        let limit_pruned_row_groups = MetricBuilder::new(metrics)
            .with_new_label("filename", Arc::clone(&shared_filename))     // <---- Only copy Arc here, not new string
            .with_type(MetricType::Summary)
            .pruning_metrics("limit_pruned_row_groups", partition);

comments.body:
We hit this one as a memory problem rather than a latency one, so here are some numbers in case they help.

**Setup:** DataFusion 54.1.0, via Sail 0.7.1.
- **Query:** `select x, count(*) … group by x` over a hive-partitioned parquet table.
- **Table:** a wide schema (488 columns, the union of many sources). Most files are small, about 1,100 files per day of data.
- **Server:** one process with a 3.9 GB cgroup limit, 4 partitions, statistics collection off.

**What we saw.** Peak memory grew linearly with the number of files scanned, about 32 MB per day (about 29 KB per file). A 27-day scan peaked at about 915 MB. A jemalloc heap profile, unsampled, put about 85% of the peak under `ParquetFileMetrics::new`. The plan's `ExecutionPlanMetricsSet` keeps every registered metric until the query ends, so these sets add up over the whole scan rather than being freed file by file.

**Two things we noticed in 54.1.0:**
1. **Duplicate registration:** each opened file gets two `ParquetFileMetrics`, one from the reader factory (`DefaultParquetFileReaderFactory::create_reader`) and one from `ParquetMorselizer::prepare_open_file`, plus a `BaselineMetrics` per file. That is about 40 filename-labelled metrics per file. Sharing a single instance per file would halve this without changing what users see, unless I'm missing a reason they're separate.
2. **#22406 doesn't change the count:** sharing the label string removes the copies, but the number of `Metric` entries still grows with the number of files.

**What we tried (local patch, not proposed as-is).** Each scan partition registers **one unlabelled** `ParquetFileMetrics` and one `BaselineMetrics` on first use. Every file opened on that partition adds to the same counters. The reader keeps its own per-file byte count, so the scan-efficiency ratio stays correct.

Results, same query and data, run alternately:

| Days scanned | 54.1.0 peak | patched peak | time |
|---|---|---|---|
| 14 | 505 MB | 188 MB | 103.5 s → 101.8 s |
| 27 | 913–921 MB | 344–350 MB | 205–231 s → 179–197 s (13–15% faster) |

Results were identical. Metrics are still registered eagerly and visible during execution, which I understand was the concern with #22353, and `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` totals don't change. **The trade-off** is that per-file metric rows and the `filename` label disappear, so this changes observable output. That's fine for us, because we only look at aggregates, but it probably shouldn't be the default.

**A possible shape upstream:** a parquet option, say `per_file_metrics` (default `true`), that falls back to per-partition metrics on scans of very many files. That, together with (1), would cover the case of wide tables with many small files.

Happy to share the patch or turn this into a PR if one of these directions sounds acceptable.
